records.source: לָמָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה תַּעֲמֹ֣ד בְּרָח֑וֹק תַּ֝עְלִ֗ים לְעִתּ֥וֹת בַּצָּרָֽה׃
records.gloss: Why, YHWH, do you stand at a distance, hide in times of trouble?
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} keep so far away? Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hide {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} when trouble comes?

L.1: Why, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} stand at a distance, [why] hide in times of trouble?

R.1: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} so far away? Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hide when we are in trouble?

decisions.choice: Why: the alphabet poem goes on
decisions.reason: Psalm 10 has no title and continues the acrostic of Psalm 9 (see 9:1): this verse begins with the letter lamed. The pattern breaks down in the middle of the psalm and returns in verses 12-17.

decisions.choice: times of trouble: the phrase of 9:10
decisions.reason: The rare phrase of 9:10, where the LORD is "a high fortress in times of trouble", returns as a complaint: in times of trouble he seems to hide.

decisions.choice: Why do you stand far off?: an honest complaint
decisions.reason: The psalmist does not doubt that God can act; he asks why he has not. Such complaints are part of faith in the Psalms (22:2; 44:24-25).

records.heading: Why do you keep so far away?

records.source: בְּגַאֲוַ֣ת רָ֭שָׁע יִדְלַ֣ק עָנִ֑י יִתָּפְשׂ֓וּ׀בִּמְזִמּ֖וֹת ז֣וּ חָשָֽׁבוּ׃
records.gloss: In [the] arrogance of [the] wicked he hotly pursues [the] afflicted; let them be caught in [the] schemes which they have devised.
pieces: In their arrogance the wicked hunt down the poor. Let them be trapped in the very schemes they have dreamed up!

L.2: In the arrogance of [the] wicked he hotly pursues [the] afflicted; let them be caught in the schemes they have devised.

R.2: Proud, wicked people chase after poor people to hurt them. Let the wicked get caught in their own evil plans!

decisions.choice: hotly pursues: chases in burning anger
decisions.reason: The verb (dalaq) means to burn, and so to chase hotly (Genesis 31:36).

decisions.choice: let them be caught: the wicked in their own schemes
alternatives: they (the afflicted) are caught in the schemes the wicked devised
decisions.reason: The verb can be a wish or a statement, and "they" can be the wicked or the poor. Read as a prayer, it asks that the wicked be caught by their own plans, as in 7:16 and 9:16; read as a statement, it describes the poor caught in the traps of the wicked.

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

records.source: כִּֽי־הִלֵּ֣ל רָ֭שָׁע עַל־תַּאֲוַ֣ת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וּבֹצֵ֥עַ בֵּ֝רֵ֗ךְ נִ֘אֵ֥ץ׀יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: For [the] wicked boasts of [the] desire of his soul, and [the] greedy one blesses; he spurns YHWH.
pieces: The wicked brag about what they crave; the greedy bless themselves while they treat {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with contempt.

L.3: For [the] wicked boasts of the desire of his soul, and the one greedy for gain blesses [himself]; he spurns {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.3: Wicked people brag about the things they want. Greedy people praise themselves, but they look down on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the greedy one blesses: praises himself, or curses
alternatives: the greedy one curses (blesses as a euphemism for curses)
decisions.reason: The words are hard to construe. "Bless" may mean that the greedy man congratulates himself, or that the wicked praise the greedy; in some places "bless" is used in place of "curse" when God is the object (Job 1:5). In each reading the line ends with contempt for the LORD.

decisions.choice: the desire of his soul: what he craves
decisions.reason: The phrase is the cravings of the self; 10:17 speaks of the "desire" of the humble with the same word.

decisions.choice: greedy for gain: one who grabs for profit
decisions.reason: The word (botsea') describes someone who seizes gain by violence or fraud (Proverbs 1:19).

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

records.source: רָשָׁ֗ע כְּגֹ֣בַהּ אַ֭פּוֹ בַּל־יִדְרֹ֑שׁ אֵ֥ין אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים כָּל־מְזִמּוֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: [The] wicked, according to the height of his nose, does not seek; there is no God [are] all his schemes.
pieces: With their noses in the air, the wicked never seek God. All their scheming says, "There is no God."

L.4: [The] wicked, in the height of his nose, does not seek [God]; "There is no God" [is] all his scheming.

R.4: Wicked people are too proud to look for God. They think, "There is no God."

decisions.choice: the height of his nose: pride
decisions.reason: A nose held high is a picture of arrogance, looking down on others.

decisions.choice: There is no God: living as if God does not matter
decisions.reason: The wicked do not argue that God does not exist; they act as if he will never see or judge (verses 11, 13). Psalm 14:1 says the same of the fool.

decisions.choice: seek: turn to God
decisions.reason: As in 9:11.

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

records.source: יָ֘חִ֤ילוּ דְרָכָ֨יו׀בְּכָל־עֵ֗ת מָר֣וֹם מִ֭שְׁפָּטֶיךָ מִנֶּגְדּ֑וֹ כָּל־צ֝וֹרְרָ֗יו יָפִ֥יחַ בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: His ways endure at all times; [on] high [are] your judgments, away from him; all his foes, he puffs at them.
pieces: Their ways always seem to succeed; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments are high above them, out of their sight; they sneer at all their enemies.

L.5: His ways prosper at all times; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments [are] on high, far from him; all his foes, he puffs at them.

R.5: Everything they do seems to go well. They do not see that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will judge them. They laugh at all their enemies.

decisions.choice: endure, prosper: stay firm and succeed
decisions.reason: The verb (chil) here means to be firm or to prosper (Job 20:21).

decisions.choice: your judgments on high, far from him: beyond his notice
decisions.reason: God's judgments are high above the wicked, out of their sight, so they live as if there were none.

decisions.choice: puffs at them: blows at them in scorn
decisions.reason: To puff (puach) at an enemy is to treat him as nothing. Psalm 12:6 uses the same verb.

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

records.source: אָמַ֣ר בְּ֭לִבּוֹ בַּל־אֶמּ֑וֹט לְדֹ֥ר וָ֝דֹ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־בְרָֽע׃
records.gloss: He says in his heart, I will not be shaken; to generation and generation [I am one] who [is] not in trouble.
pieces: "Nothing can shake me," they tell themselves; "I will never come to harm, now or ever."

L.6: He says in his heart, "I will not be shaken; for all generations I will not be in trouble."

R.6: They think, "Nothing bad will ever happen to me."

decisions.choice: says in his heart: thinks
decisions.reason: As in 4:5.

decisions.choice: to generation and generation, who not in trouble: a hard line
alternatives: he swears (reading the next verse's first word with this one)
decisions.reason: The words are compressed: "through all generations, one who is not in trouble". Some join the first word of verse 7, "a curse" or "an oath", to this verse: "he swears, 'I will not be in trouble'".

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

records.source: אָלָ֤ה פִּ֣יהוּ מָ֭לֵא וּמִרְמ֣וֹת וָתֹ֑ךְ תַּ֥חַת לְ֝שׁוֹנ֗וֹ עָמָ֥ל וָאָֽוֶן׃
records.gloss: [Of] cursing his mouth is full, and deceit and oppression; under his tongue [are] trouble and iniquity.
pieces: Their mouths are full of curses, lies and threats; they keep mischief and wrongdoing ready under the tongue.

L.7: His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and oppression; under his tongue [are] trouble and iniquity.

R.7: They are always cursing, lying and threatening people. They are ready to say hurtful, evil things.

decisions.choice: his mouth is full of cursing: quoted in Romans 3:14
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this line, in its Greek form, to describe human sin (Romans 3:14).

decisions.choice: under his tongue: ready to say, and relished
decisions.reason: What is under the tongue is kept ready and savored, like a sweet taste (Job 20:12).

decisions.choice: oppression: crushing others
decisions.reason: The word (tok) is oppression or harm done to others.

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

records.source: יֵשֵׁ֤ב׀בְּמַאְרַ֬ב חֲצֵרִ֗ים בַּֽ֭מִּסְתָּרִים יַהֲרֹ֣ג נָקִ֑י עֵ֝ינָ֗יו לְֽחֵלְכָ֥ה יִצְפֹּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: He sits in [the] ambush of villages; in hiding places he kills [the] innocent; his eyes for [the] helpless watch secretly.
pieces: They lie in wait near the villages and murder the innocent from hiding; their eyes are on the lookout for the helpless.

L.8: He sits in ambush near villages; in hiding places he kills [the] innocent; his eyes watch secretly for [the] helpless.

R.8: They hide near the villages, waiting to kill innocent people. They watch for someone who is weak and alone.

decisions.choice: villages: unwalled settlements
decisions.reason: Villages (chatserim) had no walls (Leviticus 25:31), so their people were easy prey.

decisions.choice: the helpless: a word found only in this psalm
decisions.reason: The word (chelekah) occurs only here and in verses 10 and 14. It seems to mean an unfortunate, helpless person; its exact sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

records.source: יֶאֱרֹ֬ב בַּמִּסְתָּ֨ר׀כְּאַרְיֵ֬ה בְסֻכֹּ֗ה יֶ֭אֱרֹב לַחֲט֣וֹף עָנִ֑י יַחְטֹ֥ף עָ֝נִ֗י בְּמָשְׁכ֥וֹ בְרִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: He lies in wait in hiding like a lion in its thicket; he lies in wait to seize [the] afflicted; he seizes [the] afflicted when he drags [him] in his net.
pieces: They crouch in hiding like a lion in its thicket, waiting to grab the poor; they grab them and haul them away in their nets.

L.9: He lies in wait in hiding like a lion in its thicket; he lies in wait to seize [the] afflicted; he seizes [the] afflicted, dragging [him] off in his net.

R.9: Like a lion hiding in the bushes, they wait to catch poor people. They grab them and drag them away in their nets.

decisions.choice: like a lion, in his net: hunter and beast
decisions.reason: The wicked are pictured both as a lion waiting in cover (7:3) and as a hunter with a net (9:16).

decisions.choice: he lies in wait ... he seizes: the repeated verbs
decisions.reason: The verbs are repeated (lies in wait, lies in wait; seize, seizes) to show the hunt closing in.

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

records.source: יִדְכֶּ֥ה יָשֹׁ֑חַ וְנָפַ֥ל בַּ֝עֲצוּמָ֗יו חֵ֣יל כָּאִֽים׃
records.gloss: He is crushed, he sinks down, and fall by his mighty [ones] [the] helpless.
pieces: The weak are crushed and bowed down; the helpless fall into their strong grip.

L.10: [The victim] is crushed, sinks down; and the helpless fall by his mighty [claws].

R.10: The weak are crushed and fall to the ground. The helpless are caught by their strong hands.

decisions.choice: he is crushed, sinks down: the victim, or the lion crouching
alternatives: he (the lion) crouches, bows down, and the helpless fall into his claws
decisions.reason: The verse is hard. As the Hebrew is read, the victim is crushed and sinks down, and the helpless fall under the attacker's strength. Others read the first verbs of the lion, crouching before it springs.

decisions.choice: the words as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text writes some words of this verse in one form and its notes say to read another: "and he crushes" is read "he is crushed", and one word for "the helpless" is read as two, "the strength of the dejected". The words follow the forms to be read.

decisions.choice: his mighty ones: his strong limbs or claws
decisions.reason: The word (atsum) means mighty or numerous; here probably the lion's strong claws, or the attacker's strength.

decisions.choice: the victim (L); the weak (B, R)
decisions.reason: Every level names who is crushed (m1); Literal brackets it.

records.source: אָמַ֣ר בְּ֭לִבּוֹ שָׁ֣כַֽח אֵ֑ל הִסְתִּ֥יר פָּ֝נָ֗יו בַּל־רָאָ֥ה לָנֶֽצַח׃
records.gloss: He says in his heart, God has forgotten; he has hidden his face; he will never see.
pieces: They tell themselves, "God has forgotten; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has turned {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face away and will never see."

L.11: He says in his heart, "God has forgotten; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has hidden {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will never see."

R.11: They think, "God has forgotten about us. He is not looking. He will never see what we do."

decisions.choice: he has hidden his face: he pays no attention
decisions.reason: When God hides his face he turns away and does not act (13:2; 27:9). The wicked say it with satisfaction; the psalmist said it in complaint (verse 1).

decisions.choice: forgotten: the word answered in verse 12
decisions.reason: The psalmist answers with the same verb: "do not forget the afflicted".

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

records.source: קוּמָ֤ה יְהוָ֗ה אֵ֭ל נְשָׂ֣א יָדֶ֑ךָ אַל־תִּשְׁכַּ֥ח עֲנָוִֽים׃
records.gloss: Arise, YHWH! God, lift up your hand; do not forget [the] afflicted.
pieces: Rise up, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! God, raise {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand! Do not forget those who suffer.

L.12: Arise, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! God, lift up {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand; do not forget [the] afflicted.

R.12: Get up, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! God, do something! Do not forget people who are suffering.

decisions.choice: Arise, LORD
decisions.reason: As in 3:8 (Numbers 10:35).

decisions.choice: lift up your hand: act with power
decisions.reason: A raised hand is power ready to strike or to save (Isaiah 26:11; Exodus 14:16).

decisions.choice: Arise: the alphabet returns
decisions.reason: This verse begins with the letter qof; the acrostic resumes and runs to verse 17.

decisions.choice: the afflicted: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text writes one word ("the afflicted", 'aniyyim) and its notes say to read another ("the humble", 'anavim), or the reverse; the two words are close in form and meaning, both used of the poor who depend on God. The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: do something
decisions.reason: Readable says what lifting the hand means (m2).

decisions.choice: Rise up (B); Get up (R)
decisions.reason: As in 3:8.

records.source: עַל־מֶ֤ה׀נִאֵ֖ץ רָשָׁ֥ע׀אֱלֹהִ֑ים אָמַ֥ר בְּ֝לִבּ֗וֹ לֹ֣א תִּדְרֹֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: Why has [the] wicked spurned God? He has said in his heart, You will not seek [it] out.
pieces: Why do the wicked treat God with contempt and tell themselves, "You will not call us to account"?

L.13: Why has [the] wicked spurned God? He has said in his heart, "You will not seek [it] out."

R.13: Why do wicked people look down on God? They think, "God will never punish us."

decisions.choice: seek out: call to account
decisions.reason: The verb (darash) is the one of 9:13: God "seeks" the blood of the victims. The wicked say he will not.

decisions.choice: spurned: treated with contempt
decisions.reason: The verb (na'ats) is the one of verse 3.

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

records.source: רָאִ֡תָה כִּֽי־אַתָּ֤ה׀עָ֘מָ֤ל וָכַ֨עַס׀תַּבִּיט֮ לָתֵ֪ת בְּיָ֫דֶ֥ךָ עָ֭לֶיךָ יַעֲזֹ֣ב חֵלֶ֑כָה יָ֝ת֗וֹם אַתָּ֤ה׀הָיִ֬יתָ עוֹזֵֽר׃
records.gloss: You have seen, for you — trouble and vexation you observe, to put [it] into your hand; on you the helpless leaves [himself]; [the] fatherless, you have been [his] helper.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do see! You take note of trouble and grief and take the matter into {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hands. The helpless entrust themselves to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have always helped the orphan.

L.14: You have seen, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} observe trouble and grief, to take [it] into {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand; the helpless leaves [himself] to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; for the fatherless {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been a helper.

R.14: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do see what happens! You notice when people are hurt and sad, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do something about it. Weak people trust {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to take care of them. You have always helped children who have no parents.

decisions.choice: You have seen: the answer to verse 11
decisions.reason: The wicked said, "He will never see"; the psalmist answers, "You have seen". The verse begins with the letter resh.

decisions.choice: to take it into your hand: to deal with it
decisions.reason: God takes the trouble in hand, to repay it.

decisions.choice: the fatherless, a helper: God the defender of orphans
decisions.reason: The fatherless had no one to protect their rights. God is named as their defender (Deuteronomy 10:18; Psalm 68:6).

decisions.choice: the orphan (B); children who have no parents (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the ordinary words; the point is a child with no one to protect it (m3).

records.source: שְׁ֭בֹר זְר֣וֹעַ רָשָׁ֑ע וָ֝רָ֗ע תִּֽדְרוֹשׁ־רִשְׁע֥וֹ בַל־תִּמְצָֽא׃
records.gloss: Break [the] arm of [the] wicked and [the] evil; seek out his wickedness, you will not find [it].
pieces: Break the power of the wicked and the evildoer; hunt down their wickedness until there is none left to find.

L.15: Break the arm of the wicked and the evil; seek out his wickedness [until] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} find none.

R.15: Take away the power of wicked and evil people. Punish them for every wrong they have done, until there is no evil left.

decisions.choice: the arm: strength, power
decisions.reason: The arm is power (Job 38:15); to break it is to make the wicked powerless.

decisions.choice: seek out ... you will not find: until nothing is left
alternatives: call him to account; will you not find it?
decisions.reason: God is asked to "seek out" the wickedness, the verb the wicked said he would not use (verse 13), until none can be found. The verse begins with the letter shin.

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

records.source: יְהוָ֣ה מֶ֭לֶךְ עוֹלָ֣ם וָעֶ֑ד אָבְד֥וּ ג֝וֹיִ֗ם מֵֽאַרְצֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: YHWH [is] king forever and ever; nations have perished from his land.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} reigns as King for all time; the nations are gone from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} land.

L.16: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] King forever and ever; [the] nations have perished from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} land.

R.16: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is King forever! The nations are gone from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} land.

decisions.choice: the LORD is King forever
decisions.reason: The LORD's everlasting kingship is the ground of the psalm's hope (Exodus 15:18). "King" is capitalized as a title of God, as in 5:3.

decisions.choice: have perished: as good as done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the past form: the nations that opposed the LORD are gone from his land, as at the conquest (Deuteronomy 9:3), or so certain to be that it is spoken of as done.

records.source: תַּאֲוַ֬ת עֲנָוִ֣ים שָׁמַ֣עְתָּ יְהוָ֑ה תָּכִ֥ין לִ֝בָּ֗ם תַּקְשִׁ֥יב אָזְנֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: [The] desire of [the] humble you have heard, YHWH; you make firm their heart; you incline your ear,
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have heard what the humble long for; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} steady their hearts and bend down to listen,

L.17: The desire of [the] humble {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have heard, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make their heart firm; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} incline {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear,

R.17: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear what humble people want. You give them courage. You listen to them.

decisions.choice: the desire of the humble: answered
decisions.reason: The word for desire is the one of verse 3, where the wicked boast of what they crave. The humble ('anavim) are those who depend on God. The verse begins with the letter tav, the last of the alphabet.

decisions.choice: make their heart firm: give them courage
decisions.reason: The verb (kun) means to make firm or ready; a firm heart is steady and confident (112:7).

decisions.choice: incline your ear: listen closely
decisions.reason: To incline the ear is to bend toward someone to hear.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The sentence continues into verse 18, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: לִשְׁפֹּ֥ט יָת֗וֹם וָ֫דָ֥ךְ בַּל־יוֹסִ֥יף ע֑וֹד לַעֲרֹ֥ץ אֱ֝נ֗וֹשׁ מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: to judge [the] fatherless and [the] oppressed, [so that] he will no longer again terrify, man from the earth.
pieces: to give justice to the orphan and the oppressed, so that mere mortals made of earth will strike terror no more.

L.18: to do justice for the fatherless and the oppressed, so that {{gender:mortals|man}} of the earth may terrify no more.

R.18: You will judge fairly for children without parents and for people who are treated badly. Then those who are only human will not be able to frighten them anymore.

decisions.choice: man from the earth: mortal man, or from the land
alternatives: so that no one may again drive people in terror from the land
decisions.reason: The phrase may describe the oppressor as "man who is of the earth", a mere mortal (9:21), or say that people will no longer be terrified away from the land.

decisions.choice: terrify: strike with dread
decisions.reason: The verb ('arats) is to cause terror. The psalm ends with God's justice for the weak, the answer to its opening question.

decisions.choice: mortals, with "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in 9:20.
